_about: Edit the text here, then run: python3 build/make_npc_voices.py   (only changed lines are re-made; --force redoes everything). Lykta: voice/lykta2/<id>.m4a. Villagers: voice/npc/<id>_<voice>.m4a. Real recordings: put <same name>.m4a in voice/lykta2/real/ or voice/npc/real/ and they win. A bark only plays if its text is EXACTLY a line the game shows over a villager, shopkeeper or officer (the speech bubble text); the "who" tells which kinds of speaker may say it. Changing a bark text here changes only the voice, not the bubble text in the game.

settings.note: minGapSec = the least time between two comments (any event); cool (per event, seconds) = the least time before the same event can comment again. Settings has LYKTA COMMENTS: Chatty / Quiet / Off.

lines: The square. Look at that tree. Okay, it's a very good tree. Don't tell the other trees.
Everyone ends up on the square sooner or later. Mostly to look at the tree. And to argue about parking.
Smell that? Gløgg. I can't smell. I just know it's gløgg.
The town hall has twenty-four doors and I know what's behind every one. I'm saying nothing.
If the church bells and the sleigh bells ring together, we run. Kidding. Probably.
The square! It's the heart of town. A cold, snowy, slightly crowded heart.
Listen. Bells, chatter, the odd cough. That's the sound of home.
I once spent a whole night here watching the tree light up. I never moved. I'm a lantern.
Careful with the cobbles. They've been waiting all year to trip someone.
Everyone's here. Except the witch. Mostly. Probably. Look behind you.
That's the best-lit place in town and I'm still the best light in it.
Lots of footprints in the snow. Every one a little story.
Do you smell the cinnamon? I read about cinnamon. It sounds lovely.
The town hall looks very proud today. Someone polished the doors.
I always feel a bit taller in the square. It's the echo.
If you stand still long enough, someone will tell you gossip. Try it.
So many windows. So many curtains. So many curtains twitching.
This is where the whole town meets. And where half of it forgets what it came for.
A bench! A bench with snow on it! A bench that's been waiting for us.
Look at the lights strung up everywhere. They're my cousins.
Right in the middle of it all. I get nervous in the middle of things. And excited.
This is the place for a long, slow look around. Take your time. I'm not going anywhere. I'm attached.
The square after dark. Candles, quiet, a little bit of dread. Perfect.
I like how the snow muffles everything. Even the arguments.
place_square.desc: you arrive at the town square

lines: Did the lights just... no. No, they did not.
Cold draught. Draughts are normal. Say it with me: draughts are normal.
That was the wires. Wires do that. Probably. Let's keep walking.
Hm. Did you feel that? Neither did I.
Hum something. Humming helps with draughts.
Did you see that? No. Neither did I. We're agreeing about this.
Lights do funny things in winter. Cold makes them nervous. Like me.
That was a flicker. A normal flicker. A flicker with a very bad attitude.
Don't stare at it. Whatever it is, don't stare. It's rude. And risky.
Funny. My flame leaned. Flames don't lean without a reason.
I'm sure it's nothing. Nothing is very busy in this town.
Let's pretend we heard nothing. I'm excellent at pretending.
If something taps on the glass, it's me. I'm tapping. From the inside.
Shh. Shh shh shh. It's the kind of quiet that listens back.
The shadows moved. Shadows do that. When there's a light. I'm the light. So it's me. It's probably me.
I got goosebumps. I don't have a skin. That's how bad it is.
Right. Slow steps. Pleasant thoughts. Cocoa. Think about cocoa.
Somebody's walking over my grave. I don't have a grave. Somebody's walking over my shelf.
That felt like a door opening somewhere. Somewhere that isn't a door.
Let's go where there's a crowd. A loud crowd. Please.
The cold just changed its mind about something. I didn't like it.
Humming. Humming is good. Hum a carol. Any carol.
Everything's fine. Everything's perfectly fine. Please say everything's fine.
It's only the dark. And the dark is just the day with its eyes closed.
Keep walking. Walk like you mean it. Walk like a pleasant, unbothered person.
Did the shadows just take a step? No. No, it's just me, wobbling.
threshold_glimpse.desc: the lights flickered for a moment (rare, only on a few days)

lines: The church. Nice and quiet. Suspiciously quiet. Churches are never this quiet.
Old church, old bells. If they ring on their own, we leave. That's the rule.
I like the church. Lots of candles. The candles and I have a lot in common.
Bells. Lovely bells. Terrifying bells. The bells hold both opinions.
It's so peaceful inside. I whisper in here. Even my flame whispers.
I love how the candles flicker in all the old windows. They're waving.
The steeple looks like it's poking a hole in the sky.
Old stone, old wood, old quiet. Wonderful for thinking. Awful for sudden noises.
Mind the creaky step. There's always a creaky step. Always.
Nobody has ever sneaked up on anyone in a church. The floors give you away.
I wonder what the bell would say if it could talk. Probably 'ouch'.
My cousins the candles live here. We don't discuss the family drama.
Silence is a very big sound in here, isn't it?
Do you think the ghosts here are shy? Or just very patient?
Churches smell like wax and old paper. Or so I'm told. I'm a nose-less lantern.
There's something comforting about a building older than everyone's gossip.
The graveyard's just over there. I'm not looking at it. I'm looking at my feet.
Say a little thank-you for the quiet. It's a rare thing in this town.
If the organ plays by itself, let's not stay for the encore.
Everything in here is old and holy. And I'm old and, um, nice. I fit right in.
A good place to light a candle. For luck. For courage. For me, mostly.
The snow on the roof looks like icing. Don't eat it. I mean it.
That's a troll cave. Big hole, bad smell, lots of torches. Classic troll decorating.
Trolls hate light. Which is a problem, because I am the light. Hello, trolls.
Let's go in slowly. And by slowly I mean you go first.
I can hear something breathing in there. It's the wind. It is not the wind.
Smells of wet stone and bad decisions. Welcome to the troll cave.
Those torches aren't for us. They're for the trolls to find their way home.
Hear that echo? That's one of us. Hopefully us.
Trolls are big. Trolls are grumpy. But I've heard they love a good lullaby.
I'm a very small light in a very large dark. Please don't walk ahead of me.
Is it just me or is the cave looking at us? It looks very hungry.
Let's say hello. Politely. From way back here.
Behind every rock, a troll. Or a bat. Or a troll with a bat.
Big claw marks. Probably decorative. Troll interior design.
If the ground starts rumbling, that isn't thunder. That's lunch.
My light keeps flickering near here. Or maybe I'm shaking. Hard to tell.
Trolls turn to stone in the sun. I turn to jelly in the dark. We're not so different.
A cave is just a very dark, very rude house.
The smell of troll stew. Or troll socks. Honestly can't tell.
Do trolls have doorbells? No. Do trolls have manners? Also no.
Careful where you step. Troll bones. Troll cheese. Troll homework.
I'd like to formally request we stay outside. Formal request submitted.
Something big sighed in there. I felt it in my wick.
The torches look cozy, but the shadows disagree.
Good news: the trolls are probably asleep. Bad news: probably.
place_cave.desc: you get close to a troll cave

lines: Feda. The far end of the map. She threw us a very long way, didn't she?
Feda. Population: small. Coop Prix: the best little shop in the world, and the only one.
Home of the long road. Do you remember the long road? I remember the long road.
Feda! So far away that even the snow arrives late.
Out here, the sky feels bigger. And so do the silences.
The road to Feda was long. The road home will be longer. That's how roads work.
It's cozy out here. Like the map ran out of ink and decided to nap.
Funny how the little places always have the biggest hearts. And the best shops.
I like the quiet. No traffic. No bells. Just a happy little lantern and my thoughts.
Wave at the neighbours. Both of them.
Did you buy anything at Coop Prix? You should. It's the law of Feda.
From here you can see the whole sky. And the sky can see us.
I wonder what Feda does on a Tuesday. Quietly thrives, I bet.
Look at those hills. Like sleeping giants. Let's whisper.
It took ages to get here. Let's stay for at least half an hour to make it worth it.
The wind carries things here. Smells, songs, gossip from three villages away.
Feda at night: darker than a bag of coal and about as friendly.
No witch out here. I checked all the shadows. All three.
A fine place to be a lantern. Not many lights out here, so I feel important.
I'd move here. I'd hang on the porch and watch the stars.
Every place has a secret. Feda's is probably coffee.
It's a long way from the square, but somehow it still feels like our corner of the world.
The fjord. So big. So still. So very, very deep. Let's not fall in.
I'm a lantern. Water and I do not get along. Please stay on the shore.
Pretty, isn't it? The water is like glass. Something under it is looking back.
Shh. The fjord is sleeping. Let it.
The water goes down for kilometres. I did the math. I can't do math. But kilometres.
Don't throw anything in. The fjord keeps everything. It's a collector.
I see a bright light in the water. Oh. That's me. Hello, reflection.
Wind off the fjord is like being slapped by a very cold, very polite hand.
Mountains on both sides. They're listening. They're always listening.
Lovely view. Terrible for lanterns. Salt and damp are my enemies.
Careful on the edge. The fjord only gives back what it feels like.
That mist rolling in? That's the fjord breathing.
There are boats out there somewhere. Or ghosts of boats. Equally nice to look at.
I could stare at this all night. And with no eyelids, I might.
If something rises out of the water, we're going to politely leave.
Water so still it looks like the sky fell in and stayed.
A lantern by the water is how every sad poem starts. Let's not be a sad poem.
Skipping stones is fun. Please don't skip lanterns.
The cold here has real character. And a mean streak.
Quiet in a way that makes you want to whisper secrets. Don't. It will repeat them.
I hear the tiniest ripples. A fish. Or a thought. Or both.
Let's stand here a moment. Just us, the fjord, and a bit of shivering.
A tree lot! Oh, this smells like Christmas. I think. I read about it.
Pick a good one. Not too tall, not too crooked. Nobody likes a crooked tree. Well, I do.
He sells trees by the metre. By the metre! Brilliant.
Remember, the witch hates trees too. So buying one is basically a political act.
Pine, spruce, fir. I only know the difference by how much they shed.
The smell of fresh-cut pine is the smell of 'almost Christmas'. I'm told.
Look at them all lined up, waiting to be chosen. It's like a school dance.
A tree for the house, a tree for the yard, a tree for me. I want a very small one.
Check for gaps. A good tree has no gaps. A great tree has character gaps.
That one's leaning. I like him. He's got an attitude.
Don't let him sell you the crooked one at full price. Haggle!
Trees are great. They stand still, look festive, and never argue.
Pick one with a nice top. That's where the star goes. Always the star.
The witch wants every tree chopped. We want every tree decorated. Teams are clear.
I'd decorate a tree myself, but I'd be the decoration.
Mind the sap. Sap gets everywhere. Sap is a clingy friend.
Little needles on the snow. Like green confetti. Festive litter!
Do you hear that? The trees are whispering about their new homes.
You can't go wrong. Every tree here is somebody's favourite.
Take your time. A tree is a long-term relationship.
My vote: tallest one that fits through the door. Bring a tape measure.
He's wrapped them in netting. They look like green burritos.
Imagine being a tree at the lot. Waiting. Hoping. Smelling nice. Hoping.
treelot.desc: you walk into the Christmas tree lot

lines: Carolers! Oh, they're good. A bit eerie, but good.
Listen to that. Four-part harmony at minus twelve degrees. That's dedication.
Please don't throw snowballs at the choir. I'm saying that for the record.
Tip them. The whole town likes you more for it. Well, a little.
Beautiful. Wonderful. A little bit haunting. That's carols for you.
Oh, they're doing the one with the long note. Brace yourself.
Nothing says Christmas like people singing in the cold with red noses.
I hum along. Nobody hears. I'm very good at secret humming.
That tenor deserves a raise. In cocoa.
Do they ever run out of verses? No. There's always one more verse.
Their breath makes little clouds. Little singing clouds.
I'd join in, but I only know the first two lines of everything.
You should put a coin in the hat. A big one. A noble one.
A little out of tune, a lot out of the cold. I love it.
I feel warmer when they sing. That might just be the flame.
Listen to the harmonies! Somewhere a snowflake is crying with joy.
Every carol has a story. This one is about shepherds. I think. Or sheep.
They know all the words! I know like six words. 'Ding', 'dong' and four others.
Such good voices. The witch hates them. Another reason to love them.
Do you think they'd do requests? I'd request something brave.
It's the kind of music that makes the snow fall slower.
If I could clap, I'd clap. Instead I flicker with enthusiasm.
They're so serious about it. Sheet music, scarves, frowns. Wonderful.
Stay a bit longer. This is what winter is for.
carolers.desc: a caroling group is close by

lines: That's her flat. Don't look at the window. Don't look at the window. You looked at the window.
She's down there, planning something. I can feel it in my wick.
Quietly now. She can hear a snowflake land.
Home sweet home. If home is a haunted basement with a grumpy landlady.
I used to hide in her kitchen. I will never speak of the kitchen.
The windows are dark. Which means she's definitely home.
I can smell old cabbage and bad ideas.
Her doormat says 'Go Away'. In very small writing, underneath: 'Please'.
Do you hear that cackle? No? Wait for it.
There's a candle on in the kitchen. Hmm. She doesn't like candles. Odd.
Please don't ring the bell. Please don't ring the bell. Okay, you rang the bell.
I'm only a lantern. I'm not brave. I'm just bright.
Her cat watches us from the window. He judges. Cats are the worst.
Step lightly. The stairs squeak and the walls have ears.
Everything in there is cold and slightly damp. Even the furniture.
If she opens the door, I'm hiding behind you. I'm already hiding behind you.
I don't like how clean her doorstep is. Nobody's that organised innocently.
Hear that? That's her humming. She hums when she's plotting.
I'm not scared. I'm just shaking a lot. Professionally.
I wonder if she ever eats dinner. Or just soup. Always soup.
The smell of burnt toast and mystery. That's her signature.
Don't touch the gate. It bites. I don't know how I know. I just know.
Right. We've been here long enough. We can leave now. Please.
Eyes forward, no sudden moves. We're a very boring couple of passers-by.
She's probably knitting. Evil things. With evil wool.
witchhouse.desc: you are outside the witch's house

lines: Ow! Ow ow ow. Okay. We're fine. Mostly fine. I think my glass is cracked.
That was a wall. You hit a wall. A big, solid, very visible wall.
Is the car okay? Is the wall okay? Is anyone okay? I'm just asking.
The brake is the other pedal. Just so we're clear.
Wow. They'll talk about that for three days. And they will, I've heard them.
Okay. That sound was not a good sound. That was a crunch sound.
I saw my whole wick flash before my eyes.
Maybe we should walk more. Walking has a very low crash rate.
Was that a lamp post? Sorry, lamp post. I'm family, sort of.
I'm not saying you're a bad driver. I'm saying the wall had right of way.
Everyone saw that. Everyone. Even the people who weren't there.
My light is flickering. That's just shock. Give me a second.
That's going to leave a mark. On the car. On the wall. On my self-esteem.
Hands at ten and two! Or wherever hands go. I don't have hands.
The wall didn't even flinch. Rude.
We have good insurance. Do we have insurance? Please say we have insurance.
Right. Deep breath. I don't breathe. Deep flicker.
If anyone asks, the car was already like that.
The road is wide, you know. There's plenty of it. Just, you know, use the road.
Ow. That one I felt in my handle.
I'd say 'watch out' but that's the thing that comes before this thing, not after.
Snow plus speed equals a surprise. Good to know. Writing it down. With what, I don't know.
Take a moment. Smell the burning rubber. Hm, no, that's not a nice smell.
Honestly? Kind of impressive. Not good. But impressive.
Somewhere a snowman just lost respect for you.
Next time, let's try the sneaky approach: turning.
Sirens! That's the police. That's the police and they're for us.
Okay, don't panic. Panic a little. Panic efficiently!
They really want to talk to you. Maybe it's a nice talk.
Left! No, the other left! Drive!
Blue lights! Blue lights are never a good sign. Blue lights are never a surprise party.
They're behind us. Of course they're behind us. They're always behind us.
Maybe we could just explain? No. Drive. We can explain later.
I don't want to be a lantern in a jail cell. The lighting is terrible in there.
Okay, this is fine. This is fine! This is a fun thing that's fine!
Use the side streets! The snowy ones! The narrow ones! Anywhere with fewer police!
Can they hear me? Hello, officers! We're lovely!
I told you the pavement was a bad idea. I did. Out loud. In my head.
Faster! No, slower! No, definitely faster!
My wick has never burned this fast.
Left at the church! Or right! Pick one, I'm a lantern, not a map!
Why does it always have to be sirens? Couldn't it be a nice quiet knock?
Don't worry. I'm sure it's all a misunderstanding. A big, fast, loud misunderstanding.
Think like a snowflake. Disappear.
They've got a very serious car. Ours is a bit shy.
I've got a bad feeling. In my glass. Bad glass feeling.
If we get out of this, I'm buying everyone cocoa.
Wheeeee. I mean, oh no. Both. Both at once.
It's only a chase. People have chases all the time. In movies. Which I haven't seen.
Hold on to something! Hold on to me! Not too tight, I'm glass.
They're getting closer. Everything is getting closer. Please make everything less close.
We lost them! I can't believe we lost them. Please never do that again.
Quiet now. Act natural. Be a very ordinary car.
And that, kids, is why you don't drive on the pavement.
Phew. Phew phew phew. They've gone. I think I lost a little wax.
That was close. Too close. I could count the buttons on their uniforms.
Nobody saw us. That's what we say. Nobody saw us.
Slowly, calmly, very legally. We're a very lawful car now.
I'd like to lie down. I'm a lantern. I'll hang down instead.
You're a genius! A reckless genius. But a genius!
Okay, we never speak of this. Unless there's cake. Then we speak of it a lot.
My flame is back. It went out for a second there. Only a second. Okay, three.
Next time, let's try 'not getting chased'. It has great reviews.
Excellent driving. Terrible reasons for it. But excellent driving.
They'll be looking for a big noisy car. We are now a small quiet car.
That's how it's done. Don't tell the sergeant I said that.
We got away! Can we celebrate? Quietly. Very quietly.
I need a minute. And a warm room. And possibly a candle to hold me.
Whew. And the best part? No paperwork.
Right. New life. We're good citizens now. Starting immediately. Starting in a minute.
The sirens are fading. It's the sweetest sound I've ever not heard.
I'm not even mad. I'm just relieved. And a little sweaty. Is glass sweaty?
Let's go somewhere with no police and many cookies.
You earned that. Please don't earn it again.
And the town thinks you're a slightly dodgy driver. Which is fair.
police_escape.desc: you get away from the police

lines: We're flying! We're actually flying! I'm a lantern and I'm flying!
Look at that. The whole valley. It's tiny. Everything is tiny.
Do you know how many lanterns have flown? Me. It's just me.
Please land softly. Lanterns break. I break. I'm a very breakable lantern.
Okay, okay, okay, we're high up. I'm fine. I'm a lantern, I'm supposed to be up high. Hanging from things.
Wind in my wick! Not good for the flame, great for the soul.
The church looks like a toy from here. A toy with opinions about us.
If I scream, it's joy. Mostly joy.
Birds are looking at us. They're jealous. Wave at the birds.
So this is what the roof of the world feels like. Cold. Very cold. Lovely.
Nobody told me lanterns could do this. Nobody told me anything, actually.
Don't look down. Okay, look down once. Wow. Okay, don't look down again.
I'm going to remember this when I'm old and rusty and hanging in a shed.
Fly casually. Be a normal, serious flying person. Nothing to see here, clouds.
My flame is doing a little dance. That's the altitude. Or my nerves.
Quick, name the houses you can see. I'll go first. Houses. That's all of them.
Is this what the stars see when they look at us? Because I feel judged.
Higher! No, lower! No, higher! I have no strong opinions, I just like shouting.
A lantern in the sky. People will think I'm a very small, very confused star.
Please do a loop. No wait. Don't. Yes. No. Your choice. I'm closing my glass.
The witch can't reach us up here. I checked. Twice. Don't check a third time.
Snow looks different from above. Like someone spilled the flour.
I'd wave to the town but they're tiny and I'm busy being amazed.
This is the best view I've had since I was hanging on a hook. Which was not a view.
Wheee! Sorry. That slipped out. It will slip out again.
Remember to land. Landing is half of flying. The other half is the screaming.
flying.desc: you fly (wings, jetpack, elytra, flying car)

lines: A chest! Open it, open it, open it!
Ooh. Shiny. Tell me what's inside, I can't see from here.
Treasure! Hide it from the witch.
Somebody buried this on purpose, you know. That's romantic. Or suspicious.
Chests in the hills. I never get tired of that.
What's inside? Say it's gold. Say it's cake. I'll accept either.
Somebody went to a lot of trouble hiding that. I respect the effort.
I love a chest. Chests never ask questions. They just have things.
It's heavier than it looks, isn't it? Or I'm imagining it. I'm a lantern. I can't lift anything.
Open, open, open, open. Okay. I'm calm. I'm calm.
A little sparkle, a little creak, a lot of mystery. Perfect.
If it's a mimic, I was never here.
Finders keepers! Said every lantern ever. Well, me.
Who left their treasure lying around in the snow? Honestly. Thank you, whoever you are.
Don't tell the witch about this. Don't tell anyone. Maybe tell me what's in it.
Another one! The hills are basically a giant piggy bank.
That lock had no chance. It gave up the moment it saw you.
Is it jewels? Is it socks? In this town, it could easily be socks.
I got a tingle just now. In my glass. That's how I know it's a good one.
Put it somewhere safe. Somewhere the witch doesn't look. Which is nowhere. She looks everywhere.
A chest in the snow. Mm. That's a postcard if I ever saw one.
I wonder who put it there. A secret santa with a shovel.
Each one has a little story in it. This one says 'please find me'.
You open chests like a professional. A little too gently. Be rougher.
Haha, yes! Another good find! My flame is doing a victory wiggle.
Imagine being a chest. All day waiting for one moment. And that moment was us.
Well done! One more thing crossed off the list.
Look at you, helping people. The whole town is going to love you.
I'm so proud. I'm just a lantern, but I'm proud.
Another one done. The calendar is going to be so happy.
You're good at this. Don't let it go to your head. Okay, a little.
Tick! That's one more tick. I love a tick.
Somebody out there is saying thank you right now. Maybe not out loud. But in spirit.
You did that so well. I'm dimming with pride. Wait, no, brightening.
The town is a little nicer because of you. Just a little. But a little counts.
Another job well done. Honestly, put it on a poster.
I knew you could do it. I said so. Quietly. To myself. Before you started.
Quest complete! My glass is fogging up. It's dust. It's definitely dust.
Look at that. You, helping the whole town. A real hero. A real, slightly cold hero.
That's how it's done. I'd give you a medal but I'm a lantern. Have a warm glow instead.
One for the books. Which books? The invisible books of good deeds, obviously.
The witch won't like this. Which is the best sign.
Not bad. Not bad at all. Well, actually, quite good. Fine, great.
Every little favour is a tiny candle. And you've lit another one. I approve of candles.
People will remember this. Gossip travels fast here, mostly the good kind.
Do you feel that? That warm thing in your chest? That's either pride or gløgg.
Done! Now let's do something relaxing. Like not being chased.
You're making the whole town shine. I'm jealous. Slightly. Mostly proud.
Check that off, round the corner, and onwards. The list is running scared.
If goodness were electric, we could power the whole square.
I'm writing this down in my memory. It's a small memory. But this one fits.
That was the nicest thing I've seen all day. And I see a lot, hanging here.
quest_done.desc: you finish a quest or a mission

lines: A letter from your mum! She always writes. I love it when she writes.
She sent cookies again, didn't she? ...Where do the cookies go?
Read it slowly. Mums put a lot of love in those. And a lot of cookies, apparently.
Your mum writes the best letters. I'd read every one twice.
I bet she wrote that one at the kitchen table. With a pencil. And tea.
I'm sure she says to wear a hat. Wear a hat.
Mums know everything. Even things that haven't happened yet.
Another letter! We have the best post in town.
Does she mention the cookies? I want to know about the cookies. For science.
Letters from home are better than gløgg. And I love gløgg.
She always asks if you're eating enough. And we both know the answer.
A small piece of home, folded neatly. I'd cry if I had tear ducts.
Read it out loud! No? Fine. Read it in your heart. That's also good.
She misses you. The words say 'hope you're well' but she means 'I miss you'.
Every letter smells a bit like warm kitchen, I swear. Even though I can't smell.
You're lucky. Not everyone gets a letter like this. Treasure it.
Remember to write back. Even short. Even 'hi'. Especially 'hi'.
I'd like a mum. A big warm one with a letterbox.
She can't know how brave we've been. Tell her about the lantern. Say nice things.
Hold on to that one. A letter is a hug in paper form.
Do the cookies arrive with the letters? Or separately? Very important logistics.
She always sends exactly the right words at exactly the right time.
Your mum is the real hero of this story. I'm saying nothing else.
mum.desc: you read one of Mamma's letters

lines: The bus! Ride the bus. It's slow and warm and nobody asks questions.
Do you have a ticket? I never need one. Lanterns ride free.
All aboard! Next stop: somewhere with a better view of nothing.
I like how the bus hums. Like a very large, tired cat.
Windows fogged up. Draw a face. A friendly one. Not the witch.
Look at everyone staring out of the window pretending not to stare at each other.
The seats are cold and the heater smells warm. Perfect mix.
Buses are the best place to eavesdrop. I'm not saying I do. I'm saying I'm good at it.
Beep boop. That's the doors. Beep boop.
The driver has seen things. The driver knows nothing. The driver is a professional.
Hold on to the rail. The bus likes to brake dramatically.
Snow outside, warm inside. If I could pick a motto, it'd be that.
I'm sitting on a stranger's coat. Sorry, stranger.
Quiet ride. Nobody says a word. Which means everyone is plotting something.
The bus knows every pothole by name. It's on first-name terms with them.
I always feel like we're on an adventure on a bus. Even to the shop.
Rattle rattle, clack clack. Nature's lullaby.
No driving, no police, no crashing. Let's do this more often.
Have you noticed no one on a bus ever looks happy? Except us.
The stop button is too tempting. Don't press it. Okay, press it once.
Don't fall asleep. Last time somebody did, we ended up at the depot.
Smell the damp wool. Wonderful. The smell of winter transport.
...What is THAT? Lights in the sky. Big ones. Nobody told me about lights, and I get told about everything.
Beams. Somebody is shining beams at the clouds, out there in the dark. I have so many questions.
Okay. That is either very exciting or very bad. Possibly both. I vote we go and find out.
Wait. Lights. Far away. Moving the wrong way for stars.
Something is lighting up the clouds from underneath. That seems rude. And important.
Beams of light! In the dark! Doing a slow, confident sweep. I'm a little jealous.
I don't know what that is. And I know a lot of things. A little. A bit.
Okay. Those lights have an agenda.
Do you see them too? Good. I thought it was my flame playing tricks.
A spotlight show. At this hour. In this cold. Somebody is committed.
That's not the moon. That's not the stars. That's... something with a plan.
Far off, but it feels close. Does that happen to you? Please say yes.
Strange lights are either wonderful or worrying. Rarely both. Today, both.
I'm writing this down. In my head. The ink is shaky.
Let's note it and move on. Or note it and stare. I vote stare.
Beams, beams, beams. Someone's drawing lines on the night.
Lights like that usually mean something's about to happen. I hope it's cake.
It's the sort of thing you tell your grandchildren about. If lanterns had grandchildren.
The sky is doing something and no one asked me.
Do the lights follow us? No. Wait. Maybe. Let's stop checking.
I'm trying to look unimpressed. I'm failing.
Strange glow, strange hour. A perfect fit for this town.
Whoever's up there: nice lights. Please don't land on us.
ninja_sighting.desc: you first notice the strange beams of light far away in the night sky (called by the ninja shell, never says where)

lines: Nice and smooth. I like it when we're not on fire.
Do I get a seat belt? Lanterns should get seat belts.
If you see a moose, brake. If you see a very big moose, brake and apologise.
The snow in the headlights is the prettiest thing. Pretty, and a bit hypnotic.
Mind the corners. The road doesn't care about our schedule.
I bet we could hit the shop in two minutes. If we don't crash.
This car smells like old coffee and good memories.
The heater's doing its best. So is the driver. So am I.
Left, right, left. We're a very well-coordinated team. Well, you are.
Drive like the road is a sleeping cat. Gently.
I like how the wipers go back and forth. Like they're saying 'no, no, no'.
Nothing beats a night drive. Dark road, friendly lantern, no plans.
Look at that church tower go by. It's so tall and so uninterested in us.
Radio, anyone? Or silence? I enjoy both, I'm easy.
A bump! Hold on to your hat. Hold on to my glass.
What's the speed limit here? Whatever it is, we're being brave about it.
The road ahead is so long and white. A blank page. Please don't draw a wall on it.
I wish I had a window seat. I am the window seat.
Every house we pass has someone inside having a nicer evening than us. Probably.
Our tyres are making that crunchy snow noise. Best noise in winter.
There's a certain magic to being driven. Mostly the magic of not being responsible.
I sing sometimes when we drive. Quietly. You'd never know.
A fox just looked at us. A fox and a lantern, locked eyes. Dramatic.
If the road forks, take the left. Left is almost always cozier.
Look at the hills fade into the dark. Very moody. Very Norwegian.
You drive well when you're not rushing. Remember that.
Eyes on the road. Heart on the road. Lantern on the dashboard.
Some people drive to get places. We drive to see them.
I'm going to say something supportive: you're doing very well.
Quiet drive. Fewer sirens. Great vibes.
driving.desc: you have been driving for a while (calm chatter, not during a chase)

lines: Good light today. Not as good as mine. But good.
I like the daytime. Everything's where I left it.
Do you ever stop and just look at the snow? I do. Constantly. I have nothing else to do.
Someone's made a snowman nearby. He looks smug.
I counted twelve chimneys smoking. A new record. For me.
A quiet day. Enjoy it. Quiet days are rare as hen's teeth.
In daylight my flame is just for show. Moral support, mainly.
What do you want to do first? Anything. As long as it's not dangerous.
Smells like woodsmoke, and I can't even smell. That's how strong it is.
The air is crisp. Like a good biscuit. Crisp and cold.
Pick a direction and go. The town will meet you halfway.
I see a cat. It sees me. We have an understanding.
Do you want gløgg? I think you want gløgg. I'm looking out for you.
Sunshine on snow is so bright it hurts. And I'm already bright.
The icicles are making tiny music. Drip, drip, ding.
I'm a morning lantern. I like mornings. Or at least I like the idea of mornings.
Look at the footprints. Somebody walked here, hopped there, and then changed their mind.
Everyone's busy with Christmas. Good. Busy people have fewer witch problems.
You could do a quest. Or a snowball fight. Or just wave at someone. I'm easy.
The town feels awake. You can hear it humming.
A dog barked at me earlier. I barked back. Silently. In flame.
Isn't it great how the sky changes colour and the town just keeps going?
Keep an eye out for chests. The hills are full of them.
Look at that sky. Imagine being a cloud. All that free time.
If you see anyone with a clipboard, run. Or smile. Mostly run.
Is it just me or does everything smell better with a bit of snow?
My glass is clean today. I polished it myself. Metaphorically.
Pace yourself. There's a whole advent calendar of things to do.
Today feels like a good day. I say that a lot. I'm right more often than you think.
Walking is great. Free, safe, no sirens. I approve.
idle_day.desc: daytime walking about, nothing else happening (calm chatter)

lines: It's dark. Very dark. Don't worry, I'm here. Mostly bright.
The stars are out. They're far away. Good. That's where I like my stars.
At night, everything looks like something else. A bush looks like a bear. A bear looks like a bush.
I'm the only light for miles. Feeling very responsible.
Listen to the quiet. It has a shape. And I don't like its shape.
Windows glowing in the dark. Every one a tiny lantern's cousin.
Is it just me or are the shadows longer than usual?
The moon's out. It's like me, but bigger and colder.
Walk where it's bright. Streetlights are our friends.
I hear a twig snap. It's probably nothing. I'm still going to hide behind you.
Night is my favourite time. I get to do my best work. Be bright.
There's a particular smell to snow at night. Cold and clean and a bit secret.
If you hear footsteps behind us, they're probably ours. Hopefully ours.
The dark has a lot of corners. I'd avoid all of them.
Every lamp post says goodnight to us as we pass. Politely.
My flame is steady. Don't look at my flame. Steady, steady.
I like how the snow glows at night. Like it's saving up light for later.
Chimney smoke against the stars. That's postcard material.
Do you hear a faint ringing? Or is that my nerves? Probably nerves.
Maybe tonight we find something wonderful. Or maybe we find a ghost. 50-50.
I've got a great idea: let's stay in the lit areas.
A whole town asleep. Shhh. Let's not wake it.
Every shadow has a story. Most of them end badly.
I can do spooky voices. Do you want me to? No? Good. I was shaking.
The best thing about the night: the gløgg tastes better. The worst: the witch is more awake.
An owl! Or a very small ghost with feathers.
Walking at night is just a long bedtime story with legs.
The cold has teeth tonight. Gentle ones. But teeth.
Keep going. Keep humming. Keep close to the lantern.
It's very peaceful. A bit too peaceful. Peaceful like someone holding their breath.
idle_night.desc: night time walking about, nothing else happening (calm, a bit spooky chatter)

lines: Snowing! Look at it! It's like the sky is shaking out a pillow.
Each flake is different. Someone counted. I don't know who. A very patient someone.
Careful, my flame hates snow. We have a complicated relationship.
It's coming down so hard I can barely see the road. Or the other road. Or the third road.
If we stand still, we'll turn into snowmen. Let's keep moving.
Snow on the hat, snow on the boots, snow on my glass. Snow everywhere. Lovely.
Listen to the silence. The snow is eating all the noise.
I think the sky is trying to bury us in sparkles.
Quick, catch a flake on your tongue. Tell me what it tastes like.
A blizzard is just the weather being dramatic. I respect it.
My light looks great in the snow. Little glowy halos on everything.
Snowdrifts are the best. And the worst. Depends on whether you're in one.
The whole town is turning into a postcard. A frosty, rather windy postcard.
Don't mind me, I'll just be here, melting a little at the edges.
Everything is quieter in the snow. Even the witch. Allegedly.
Look how the flakes dance around the lamp posts. They're showing off.
Wrap up warm. Your nose is the colour of a cherry.
The wind is whistling a tune. It's quite catchy actually.
Everything smells like cold. And cold doesn't smell. That's how much snow there is.
Snow in the air, snow in the trees, snow in places snow shouldn't be. Brilliant.
I like the sound of crunching boots. It's a rhythm. A cold rhythm.
Let's pretend it's a snow globe. We're the tiny people. Someone's shaking us.
Big flakes. Sloppy, soggy, happy flakes.
Footprints fill up quickly in this. Nobody can follow us. Take that, witch.
It's the kind of snow you wish you had a sledge for.
The snow's piling up on the roofs. Houses are wearing marshmallow hats.
If I could catch a snowflake, I'd keep it. Forever. In my pocket. If I had pockets.
The sky's turned white. And so has the ground. It's like being inside a cloud.
Hot cocoa in this weather? Yes please. Go find some.
Winter is here and it's showing off.
idle_snow.desc: it is snowing hard while you walk about (calm chatter)

lines: Her flat. The window has curtains now. Flowery ones. I have questions about the curtains.
Smells of cinnamon and wool. Last month it was cabbage and bad ideas. I am adjusting.
The doormat says Welcome. I checked it for tricks. There are none. That is suspicious in itself.
There is a doily in the window. A doily. I did not know this house was allowed to have one.
I used to hide in that kitchen. Now it has a kettle and a tea cosy shaped like a cat. Growth, I suppose.
Quietly now. Not from danger. She is probably napping, and she bakes when she wakes up.
The cellar door is just a door now. Do not tell the door I said that.
Smoke from the chimney. A normal amount. I keep waiting for it to spell something.

nutter.desc: rare batshit remark (own pool, own bag; only lines for the current day or earlier; see job lyktanutters)
lines: I counted the snowflakes. There are too many. Somebody is cheating.
Do not look at the left ones. Look at the right ones. The left ones know.
I dreamed I was a toaster. Best night of my life.
If the road asks you a question, say yes. The road hates a no.
I have decided the moon is a very large coin and nobody is spending it.
Your shadow is a quarter second late. I am not worried. I am being professional.
Say the word gravy to the nearest tree. Go on. Watch what it does. Nothing. Suspicious.
I made a friend today. It was a draught. We are no longer speaking.
Somebody put lasers in the forest. I have questions and a small grudge.
If you jump high enough you are technically a bird with bad manners.
I am a light. I am also, secretly, a very tired candle in a lantern costume.
Beep. That was not me. I just wanted to see who flinched.
I read a letter that was not ours. I will say nothing. I will say nothing VERY loudly.
Cats are small landlords. Pay the rent. Do not ask where it goes.
There is a smell of wool and bad decisions. Follow it. Or do not. I am a lantern, not a mum.
I lost a minute yesterday. I think a goose has it.
I blinked. Half a second is missing. I want it back. I know who has it.
Nobody panic, but the dark just waved. Somebody wave back. Politely.
I have started naming the stars. This one is Kevin. He owes me money.
If the lights go out, do not shout. Whisper. Whispering is louder in the dark. Science.
Snow is just the sky being nervous.
I have decided to forgive Tuesday. Wednesday is on a final warning.
Somebody here is humming a tune that does not exist yet. I am keeping my eye on the tune.
Do you ever feel like the town is looking at you? No? Just me? Fine. Great. Lovely.
A letter from your mum, and cookies. I am going to be nice about this. I will be nice for exactly four seconds.
I could eat a pepperkake. I have no mouth. I have a plan.
Your mum writes to you with ink. I glow at you with feelings. We are not the same.
If I ever become a ghost I would like to haunt a biscuit tin. A modest ambition.
There is a hole in the floor. Holes are just floors that gave up.
Down there something is counting. It is on twelve. Do not give it a thirteen.
I am not scared. I am just cautiously glowing in a very stern way.
A trapdoor is a door that has made an unusual life choice.
I have never trusted a cupboard. It has too many opinions on the inside.
The recipe card is written in a hand that knows things. Handwriting can know things.
I am being completely normal. Look how normal I am. Look at my normal glow.
Today I am going to be extremely brave. From behind you.
Another batch is thinner. The cookie is losing a war and nobody is telling the cookie.
I counted the doors in town. There is one more than yesterday. I am not saying who.
If the wind sounds like a whisper, it is the wind. If the whisper sounds like the wind, run.
Somebody has been in the post. Somebody with sticky fingers and a broom problem.
The dough looked at me. I looked back. We have an understanding.
Bake the thing. Bake the thing. Bake the thing. The oven is a kind god.
I put a little bell on everything. It is for my peace of mind, and for their screams.
A gingerbread man has never once looked behind him. Think about that.
The air tastes like a fire alarm in a library. Today is a day.
If anyone offers you tea today, ask what is in it. Then ask again, slower.
I am glowing at maximum. That is not a metaphor. That is a warning.
Whatever happens, I want you to know I was always going to be this dramatic.
A girl with candles on her head is the most normal thing that has happened all week.
Somebody has been very kind to me and I do not know what to do with my face.
Today the dark feels thinner. I am a lantern. I notice thin dark. It is my entire job.
I think I like magic. I think magic likes me back. It sent a rude little spark. I count it as love.
Go faster. No, the OTHER faster.
Racing is just falling forwards with confidence.
I am going to cheer. I am a lantern. My cheering is a lot of light and a little scream.
Whoever wins, I will say I had faith. Whoever loses, I will say I was always right.
The sky is throwing rocks. Rude. Beautiful. Rude.
Make a wish. I have already made yours. Sorry. It was mostly about me.
If a rock falls from space and it is shaped like a spoon, I am keeping it.
I just want you to know that tonight the stars are doing the most.
Men in white suits asked me to move. I am a lantern. I move for no one. I moved.
There is tape in the street. Tape has never solved anything. It has made a lot of people feel important.
Nobody has told us anything. Which means everybody knows something.
I would like to speak to whoever is in charge of the weather. I have notes.
Something under the town is humming a note I almost know.
A pulse. A pulse. A pulse. A pulse. Are you counting? You should count.
Do not stare at the thing that stares back. Stare at the thing next to it. Casual.
I want it noted that I said hello first. The hum did not say hello back.
Two chiefs. One table. Eleven thousand opinions about porridge.
The nisse are tiny and furious and I respect them more than I respect most things.
A peace treaty is just two people agreeing to stop being right at each other.
If anyone throws a spoon, it is not me. I have no arms. I have very strong intentions.
A real plane. In a village. I checked the cockpit for a dog. There was no dog. I am disappointed.
Fly it over town and wave at everyone. They will wave back. Or throw things. Both are love.
I have always wanted to be sucked into an engine. That sounded better in my head.
Do not look down. Look sideways. Sideways is a far less judgemental direction.
It is very quiet. I do not like quiet. Say something. Say ANYTHING.
The quiet has a smell, and the smell is the end of a sentence.
I tried to hum and the dark ate it. I am hurt. I am also impressed.
If you hear nothing, that is the sound. Do not tell it I said so.
Fifteen piles of rocks. We are doing a rock thing. I am so proud of us.
The longest night. I am going to be as bright as a lantern can be. That is the whole job.
Light a candle for somebody who is not here. Then light one for a pickle. The pickle needs it too.
If the dark ever asks what I am afraid of, I will say socks. It will never see it coming.
The men in white suits closed the case. They were wrong, loudly, and in writing.
Nobody likes a tidy ending that does not fit. I have kept the crumbs.
I feel strange. Like a candle the day after a birthday.
If you find a clue today, bring it to me. If you find a feeling, keep that one. It is heavier.
The gingerbread house is bigger than yesterday. It is not me. It is not me.
Something woke up and it is a bit grumpy and extremely large. I made it a very small tea.
I am going to say something wise now. Okay, I forgot. Carry on.
Tomorrow is a big day. I am going to be fine. I am a light. I am simply a light. Do not look at me.
Tonight a very large lizard wants a word. I have prepared a speech and a small hat.
If this is the last night, I would like it noted that I was gorgeous the entire time.
Whatever you do, do not blink first. Blinking is for people with no plan.
I have loved this. I have loved all of it. Even Kevin. Especially Kevin.

barks.text: Har du hørt om han som kjørte over julenissen?
De sier han tok julenissen rett på fortauet...
Julenissen skal ikke være fornøyd. Bilisten heller ikke, tipper jeg.
Har du sett bilen hans? Sånn kjører man ikke i Kvinesdal!
Noen dytta borti en stakkar med bilen, midt i gata!
Hørte du? En bil tok en fotgjenger utenfor bakeriet.
Pass deg, det går en farlig sjåfør løs i sentrum.
Hørte du smellet? En bil rett i veggen!
Han kjørte inn i et gjerde i går. Gjerdet har det bra.
To biler kolliderte ved torget. Typisk.
Det smalt i sentrum i går. Bare bildeler igjen.
Kjører man sånn på fortauet? PÅ FORTAUET!
Se opp for han med bilen, han kjører som om vi er kjegler.
Jeg måtte hoppe i snøen for en bil i går.
Politiet jagde en bil gjennom sentrum! Jeg har det på film.
Sirener hele kvelden. Jeg trodde det var julemusikk.
Har du sett politibilene? Noen har vært uskikkelige.
Noen skjøt opp raketter midt i sentrum. Hunden min er fortsatt under senga.
Den smellen! Jeg trodde det var krig.
Nyttårsaften er jo ikke før om en måned...
Det var et TROLL i sentrum. Et TROLL!
Jeg så et troll. Nei, jeg har ikke drukket gløgg.
Jeg så deg på Kvinesdal Nytt!
Du er på TV nå, vet du. Leservideo!
Naboen min har lagt ut filmen. Alle har sett den.
Har du hørt? Noen hjalp gamle Olga med handleposene!
Fin fyr, han der. Han ga meg til og med en pepperkake.
Det går en snill en rundt i byen. Si det til ingen.
Der går han. Ikke se i øynene hans.
Du er det beste som har skjedd Kvinesdal siden brunosten.
Dette må jeg ha på film!
Alle kommer til å se dette!
God jul! The julekake just came out of the oven.
Velkommen! The kakao comes with whipped cream.
Grab a table, I'll bring it over.
Hei! Grandiosa is on offer this week.
Hei! Pølse i lompe? The grill is hot.
Smågodt is half price on Saturdays!
Vi pakker det i nett, så er det lettere å bære.
Den holder nåler helt til nyttår.
Welcome in! Grab some shoes at the desk.
God kveld! Sko får du hos Arild.
Skal vi ta air hockey etterpå?
Jeg slo deg sist, husker du?
These shoes are way too small.
Du fusker, du sto på streken!
En cola og en pølse, takk.
Ha det bra, og kom igjen!
One more credit and I get the high score!
Har du hørt det? Kvinesdal har fått sin egen ninjabane!
De sier noen har bygd en hinderløype. Ingen vet hvem.
Jeg hørte det er en ninjabane. Ingen vil si hvor den er. Typisk.
Lysene på himmelen i natt! Så du dem? Lange strålekastere!
Hunden min bjeffet på lysene hele natta.
Noen sier det er rakettene til julenissen. Jeg tror det er noe større.
Jeg så en lysstråle som svingte rundt og rundt. Jeg ble helt svimmel.
Naboen min sier han vet hvor den er. Han lyver. Han vet ingenting.
Første som finner ninjabanen får en premie, sier de. Jeg leter allerede!
Jeg har lett i tre dager. Bare snø. Og en elg.
Nå ser man lysene fra kjøkkenvinduet. Jeg setter meg ned med kaffen og ser på.
Alle spør hvor den er. Ingen svarer. Det er så spennende!

storyGossip._about: Story gossip by advent day (plan 2.3, PROPOSED text). Wiring: the __TOWN gossip pool picks these lines on the matching day (storyspine/townlife). Not voiced yet.
7: Somebody down your street is eating the post. Nobody will say who.
8: The witch's flat has a cellar. Nobody goes near the cellar. Nobody has ever been near the cellar.
13: Quiet, isn't it? Nobody is shouting through the walls. I miss it, a little.
15: Did you see the sky? Don't look up at it. Look at your feet, like a sensible person.
16: Men in black coats up at the crater. They are very polite. That is what worries me.
17: The lights went grey last night. Just for a minute. Nobody says it, but we all counted.
20: Something in the crater. Gunnar swears he saw it blink.
22: Warm is a team sport, my grandmother said. Then she said it again, just in case.
